reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Every English line of the chapter was read against the Greek. No line adds interpretive content, uses Raëlian-canon vocabulary (no Elohim, Yahweh, craft, creators, ray, planet, Eternals), or resolves an ambiguity in the canon's direction. Each Wheel of Heaven reading sits in its own paragraph headed 'reception note, not a translation claim'. The two lines that coincide with the canon's French were tested specifically: 2:2/2:9 'at its rising' (BDAG ἀνατολή 1 cites both verses; NAB 1970, NRSV, ESV) and 26:53 'put at my disposal' (BDAG παρίστημι 1a cites the verse; NASB identical wording). In both the lexical ground is real and independent of the canon, so neither is lens leakage.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts were formed from the Greek, the chapter JSON, the overlay and the central diff before the escalation report (wave-m2-editor-report.md) was opened. The report added no information that changes a verdict. It repeats the RSV attribution for 2:2/9 ('RSV, NRSV, NAB'), which this review corrects. Its ten founder-preference points are answered in founderDecisionRecommendations, and its follow-ups (17:21; 17:22; comma/colon in 25 and 28; the 6:13 'testing' wording in central) are endorsed as later-pass items.

founderDecisionRecommendations.1-angelos-angel: Endorse. ἄγγελος is the technical term for a heavenly envoy in first-century Jewish Greek (BDAG s.v. 2); published Mt 1, 13, 25, 28, Acts 12 and the Revelation wave all print 'angel', so the Greek NT is already harmonized in practice. Promote jointly with Revelation as a central Greek-NT convention; keep 'messenger of YHWH' for Hebrew malʾāḵ.
founderDecisionRecommendations.2-naos-sanctuary: Endorse for Matthew. The naos/hieron distinction is lexical (BDAG; Josephus) and NRSV marks it in 23:16-35. 27:5 keeps Matthew's crux honestly (and, to my reading, restores the ASV's own 'sanctuary'). If promoted, scope it to books with both terms; Revelation's 'temple' for ναός is defensible because it has no ἱερόν.
founderDecisionRecommendations.3-23:14-no-paragraph: Endorse. SBLGNT has no 23:14; the Byzantine text is quoted in full at 23:13 with witnesses, as the 6:13b precedent and the Revelation ruling C require. Recommend a later pass bring the stable 17:21 into line: its bracketed Greek is not SBLGNT text, so drop the paragraph and move the Byzantine wording into the 17:20 commentary.
founderDecisionRecommendations.4-colon-convention: Endorse (punctuation only; applied without exception in the wave). Harmonize published 25 and 28 in a later pass.
founderDecisionRecommendations.5-magi: Endorse. 'magi' is the standard scholarly rendering (BDAG; Brown; Powell) and NIV/NAB usage; 'wise men' is noted.
founderDecisionRecommendations.6-faithfulness-23:23: Endorse. BDAG lists Mt 23:23 under πίστις 1a 'faithfulness, reliability'; NIV and ESV render so; the Mic 6:8 triad is conduct.
founderDecisionRecommendations.7-put-at-my-disposal-26:53: Endorse. BDAG παρίστημι 1a cites this verse for 'put at someone's disposal', and the NASB prints exactly 'put at My disposal'; the ground is independent of the canon's French, and the coincidence is disclosed.
founderDecisionRecommendations.8-at-its-rising-2:2,9: Endorse. BDAG ἀνατολή 1 cites both verses; NAB (1970, before TBWTT) and NRSV read 'at its rising', ESV 'when it rose'. Correct the RSV attribution (the RSV reads 'in the East').
founderDecisionRecommendations.9-defiles-a-person: Endorse. The article with ἄνθρωπος is generic; the canon's own French « l'homme » is generic too, so the line follows the sense the canon intends rather than the English edition's 'the man'.
founderDecisionRecommendations.10-tempted-4:1: Endorse. Agent-driven 'tempted'/'the tempter' is BDAG's and the versions' reading with the devil as agent, and agrees with published 6:13; the test reading (Gerhardsson; canon « mis à l'épreuve ») is properly in commentary. Optionally align the chapter 4 title ('The testing in the wilderness') with the line.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς λόγους τούτους, μετῆρεν ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ ὅρια τῆς Ἰουδαίας πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου.
paragraphs.translit: kai egeneto hote etelesen ho iēsous tous logous toutous, metēren apo tēs galilaias kai ēlthen eis ta horia tēs ioudaias peran tou iordanou.

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these words, he departed from Galilee and came into the region of Judea beyond the Jordan.

notes.official: 'when Jesus had finished these words': the formula that closes each of Matthew's five discourses (7:28; 11:1; 13:53; 19:1; 26:1).

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοί, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτοὺς ἐκεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēkolouthēsan autō ochloi polloi, kai etherapeusen autous ekei.

i18n.en: And great crowds followed him, and he healed them there.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ Φαρισαῖοι πειράζοντες αὐτὸν καὶ λέγοντες· Εἰ ἔξεστιν ἀνθρώπῳ ἀπολῦσαι τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ κατὰ πᾶσαν αἰτίαν;
paragraphs.translit: kai prosēlthon autō pharisaioi peirazontes auton kai legontes· ei exestin anthrōpō apolysai tēn gynaika autou kata pasan aitian;

i18n.en: And Pharisees came to him, testing him and saying: "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any cause?"

notes.official: *peirazontes auton* 'testing him': here *peirazō* means probing with a question, as at 16:1 and 22:35, and is rendered 'test' (`peirazo-peirasmos-tempt-test-matthew`). *kata pasan aitian* 'for any cause' alludes to the debate between the schools of Hillel and Shammai over the grounds for divorce in Deut 24:1 (m. Giṭ. 9:10).

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε ὅτι ὁ κτίσας ἀπʼ ἀρχῆς ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐποίησεν αὐτοὺς
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen· ouk anegnōte hoti ho ktisas apʼ archēs arsen kai thēly epoiēsen autous

i18n.en: And he answered and said: "Have you not read that he who created them from the beginning made them male and female,

notes.official: *ho ktisas* 'he who created' (critical text, with Vaticanus). The Byzantine text, with Sinaiticus and C, reads *ho poiēsas* 'he who made' (KJV 'he which made them'), the verb of Gen 1:27 LXX (`critical-text-baseline-and-byzantine-variant-recording-matthew`). *arsen kai thēly epoiēsen autous* 'made them male and female' quotes Gen 1:27 LXX.

paragraphs.text: καὶ εἶπεν· Ἕνεκα τούτου καταλείψει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ κολληθήσεται τῇ γυναικὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν;
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen· heneka toutou kataleipsei anthrōpos ton patera kai tēn mētera kai kollēthēsetai tē gynaiki autou, kai esontai hoi dyo eis sarka mian;

i18n.en: and said: 'For this reason a man shall leave his father and his mother and shall be joined to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh'?

notes.official: Gen 2:24 LXX. *hoi dyo* 'the two' is in the LXX but not in the MT. The colon follows this wave's convention (`speech-introduction-colon-convention-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: ὥστε οὐκέτι εἰσὶν δύο ἀλλὰ σὰρξ μία. ὃ οὖν ὁ θεὸς συνέζευξεν ἄνθρωπος μὴ χωριζέτω.
paragraphs.translit: hōste ouketi eisin dyo alla sarx mia. ho oun ho theos synezeuxen anthrōpos mē chōrizetō.

i18n.en: So they are no longer two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, let no one separate."

notes.official: *anthrōpos mē chōrizetō* 'let no one separate': *anthrōpos* is generic and contrasted with *ho theos*, so the line reads 'no one'; the draft and the ASV had 'let not man' / 'let no man' (`anthropos-generic-people-convention-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Τί οὖν Μωϋσῆς ἐνετείλατο δοῦναι βιβλίον ἀποστασίου καὶ ἀπολῦσαι αὐτήν;
paragraphs.translit: legousin autō· ti oun mōysēs eneteilato dounai biblion apostasiou kai apolysai autēn;

i18n.en: They say to him: "Why then did Moses command to give a certificate of divorce and to divorce her?"

notes.official: Deut 24:1. *biblion apostasiou* 'a certificate of divorce', as in the published 5:31.

paragraphs.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὅτι Μωϋσῆς πρὸς τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν ὑμῶν ἐπέτρεψεν ὑμῖν ἀπολῦσαι τὰς γυναῖκας ὑμῶν, ἀπʼ ἀρχῆς δὲ οὐ γέγονεν οὕτως.
paragraphs.translit: legei autois hoti mōysēs pros tēn sklērokardian hymōn epetrepsen hymin apolysai tas gynaikas hymōn, apʼ archēs de ou gegonen houtōs.

i18n.en: He says to them: "Because of your hardness of heart Moses permitted you to divorce your wives; but from the beginning it has not been so.

paragraphs.text: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ μὴ ἐπὶ πορνείᾳ καὶ γαμήσῃ ἄλλην μοιχᾶται καὶ ὁ ἀπολελυμένην γαμήσας μοιχᾶται.
paragraphs.translit: legō de hymin hoti hos an apolysē tēn gynaika autou mē epi porneia kai gamēsē allēn moichatai kai ho apolelymenēn gamēsas moichatai.

i18n.en: And I say to you: whoever divorces his wife, except for unchastity, and marries another, commits adultery; and he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery."

notes.official: *mē epi porneia* 'except for unchastity': *porneia* is rendered 'unchastity' as in the published 5:32 (KJV 'fornication'; NRSV 'unchastity'). SBLGNT includes the final clause *kai ho apolelymenēn gamēsas moichatai* 'and he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery'. Vaticanus and others read *parektos logou porneias poiei autēn moicheuthēnai* 'except on the ground of unchastity, makes her commit adultery', assimilating to 5:32; Sinaiticus, Bezae and others omit the final clause (Metzger, Textual Commentary, ad loc.; `critical-text-baseline-and-byzantine-variant-recording-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί· Εἰ οὕτως ἐστὶν ἡ αἰτία τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μετὰ τῆς γυναικός, οὐ συμφέρει γαμῆσαι.
paragraphs.translit: legousin autō hoi mathētai· ei houtōs estin hē aitia tou anthrōpou meta tēs gynaikos, ou sympherei gamēsai.

i18n.en: The disciples say to him: "If such is the case of the man with his wife, it is better not to marry."

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐ πάντες χωροῦσι τὸν λόγον τοῦτον ἀλλʼ οἷς δέδοται.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen autois· ou pantes chōrousi ton logon touton allʼ hois dedotai.

i18n.en: But he said to them: "Not all can receive this saying, but only those to whom it has been given.

paragraphs.text: εἰσὶν γὰρ εὐνοῦχοι οἵτινες ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς ἐγεννήθησαν οὕτως, καὶ εἰσὶν εὐνοῦχοι οἵτινες εὐνουχίσθησαν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ εἰσὶν εὐνοῦχοι οἵτινες εὐνούχισαν ἑαυτοὺς διὰ τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν. ὁ δυνάμενος χωρεῖν χωρείτω.
paragraphs.translit: eisin gar eunouchoi hoitines ek koilias mētros egennēthēsan houtōs, kai eisin eunouchoi hoitines eunouchisthēsan hypo tōn anthrōpōn, kai eisin eunouchoi hoitines eunouchisan heautous dia tēn basileian tōn ouranōn. ho dynamenos chōrein chōreitō.

i18n.en: For there are eunuchs who were born so from their mother's womb; and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by people; and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of the heavens. The one who is able to receive it, let him receive it."

notes.official: 'eunuchs who were made eunuchs by people' (*hypo tōn anthrōpōn*, generic). 'for the sake of the kingdom of the heavens' (`kingdom-of-heaven-basileia-tōn-ouranōn-mt-distinctive-cross-corpus-hebrew-malkhut-shamayim`).

paragraphs.text: Τότε προσηνέχθησαν αὐτῷ παιδία ἵνα τὰς χεῖρας ἐπιθῇ αὐτοῖς καὶ προσεύξηται· οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἐπετίμησαν αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: tote prosēnechthēsan autō paidia hina tas cheiras epithē autois kai proseuxētai· hoi de mathētai epetimēsan autois.

i18n.en: Then little children were brought to him, so that he might lay his hands on them and pray; but the disciples rebuked them.

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία καὶ μὴ κωλύετε αὐτὰ ἐλθεῖν πρός με, τῶν γὰρ τοιούτων ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de iēsous eipen· aphete ta paidia kai mē kōlyete auta elthein pros me, tōn gar toioutōn estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn.

i18n.en: But Jesus said: "Let the little children be, and do not forbid them to come to me; for to such as these belongs the kingdom of the heavens."

notes.official: 'to such as these belongs the kingdom of the heavens' (`kingdom-of-heaven-basileia-tōn-ouranōn-mt-distinctive-cross-corpus-hebrew-malkhut-shamayim`).

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῖς ἐπορεύθη ἐκεῖθεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai epitheis tas cheiras autois eporeuthē ekeithen.

i18n.en: And he laid his hands on them and went on from there.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἰδοὺ εἷς προσελθὼν αὐτῷ εἶπεν· Διδάσκαλε, τί ἀγαθὸν ποιήσω ἵνα σχῶ ζωὴν αἰώνιον;
paragraphs.translit: kai idou heis proselthōn autō eipen· didaskale, ti agathon poiēsō hina schō zōēn aiōnion;

i18n.en: And behold, one came to him and said: "Teacher, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?"

notes.official: *Didaskale* 'Teacher' (critical text). The Byzantine text and the KJV read *Didaskale agathe* 'Good Master', from Mark 10:17 and Luke 18:18; the variant is linked to the one in 19:17. *zōēn aiōnion* 'eternal life' (`aiōnios-mt-25-41-46-eternal-vs-age-pertaining-cross-corpus`; overlay `aionios-eternal-vs-age-pertaining-translation-convention`).

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τί με ἐρωτᾷς περὶ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ; εἷς ἐστιν ὁ ἀγαθός· εἰ δὲ θέλεις εἰς τὴν ζωὴν εἰσελθεῖν, τήρησον τὰς ἐντολάς.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen autō· ti me erōtas peri tou agathou; heis estin ho agathos· ei de theleis eis tēn zōēn eiselthein, tērēson tas entolas.

i18n.en: And he said to him: "Why do you ask me about what is good? One there is who is good. But if you wish to enter into life, keep the commandments."

notes.official: *Ti me erōtas peri tou agathou? heis estin ho agathos* 'Why do you ask me about what is good? One there is who is good.' The Byzantine text and the KJV read *Ti me legeis agathon? oudeis agathos ei mē heis ho theos* 'Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God', which harmonizes with Mark 10:18 and Luke 18:19. The critical reading, supported by Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, D and L, is the harder one: Matthew seems to have avoided the implication that Jesus declines to be called good (Metzger, Textual Commentary, ad loc.; `critical-text-baseline-and-byzantine-variant-recording-matthew`). 'One there is who is good' refers to God.

paragraphs.text: λέγει αὐτῷ· Ποίας; ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Τὸ Οὐ φονεύσεις, Οὐ μοιχεύσεις, Οὐ κλέψεις, Οὐ ψευδομαρτυρήσεις,
paragraphs.translit: legei autō· poias; ho de iēsous eipen· to ou phoneuseis, ou moicheuseis, ou klepseis, ou pseudomartyrēseis,

i18n.en: He says to him: "Which ones?" And Jesus said: "'You shall not murder; You shall not commit adultery; You shall not steal; You shall not bear false witness;

notes.official: 19:18-19 quote the second table of the Decalogue (Exod 20:12-16; Deut 5:16-20) and add Lev 19:18 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself', a combination specific to Matthew.

paragraphs.text: Τίμα τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα, καὶ Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.
paragraphs.translit: tima ton patera kai tēn mētera, kai agapēseis ton plēsion sou hōs seauton.

i18n.en: Honor your father and your mother'; and, 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself.'"

paragraphs.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ νεανίσκος· Πάντα ταῦτα ἐφύλαξα· τί ἔτι ὑστερῶ;
paragraphs.translit: legei autō ho neaniskos· panta tauta ephylaxa· ti eti hysterō;

i18n.en: The young man says to him: "All these I have kept; what do I still lack?"

paragraphs.text: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Εἰ θέλεις τέλειος εἶναι, ὕπαγε πώλησόν σου τὰ ὑπάρχοντα καὶ δὸς πτωχοῖς, καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν οὐρανοῖς, καὶ δεῦρο ἀκολούθει μοι.
paragraphs.translit: ephē autō ho iēsous· ei theleis teleios einai, hypage pōlēson sou ta hyparchonta kai dos ptōchois, kai hexeis thēsauron en ouranois, kai deuro akolouthei moi.

i18n.en: Jesus said to him: "If you wish to be perfect, go, sell your possessions and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in the heavens; and come, follow me."

notes.official: *teleios* 'perfect', the word of 5:48 ('You shall be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect'). *thēsauron en ouranois* 'treasure in the heavens' keeps the Greek plural; the published 6:20 has the singular *en ouranō* 'in heaven'.

paragraphs.text: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ νεανίσκος τὸν λόγον ἀπῆλθεν λυπούμενος, ἦν γὰρ ἔχων κτήματα πολλά.
paragraphs.translit: akousas de ho neaniskos ton logon apēlthen lypoumenos, ēn gar echōn ktēmata polla.

i18n.en: But when the young man heard the saying, he went away grieving, for he had many possessions.

paragraphs.text: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πλούσιος δυσκόλως εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν·
paragraphs.translit: ho de iēsous eipen tois mathētais autou· amēn legō hymin hoti plousios dyskolōs eiseleusetai eis tēn basileian tōn ouranōn·

i18n.en: And Jesus said to his disciples: "Amen I say to you, it is with difficulty that a rich man will enter into the kingdom of the heavens.

notes.official:
*plousios dyskolōs eiseleusetai* 'it is with difficulty that a rich man will enter': *plousios* is an individual, so 'a rich man' (`anthropos-generic-people-convention-matthew`). 'the kingdom of the heavens' (`kingdom-of-heaven-basileia-tōn-ouranōn-mt-distinctive-cross-corpus-hebrew-malkhut-shamayim`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 5) quotes 19:23 (« un riche entre difficilement dans le règne des cieux ») in its critique of the Church's wealth. The canon's 'the kingdom of the heavens' (« le règne des cieux ») matches the Greek plural that the line keeps.

paragraphs.text: πάλιν δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, εὐκοπώτερόν ἐστιν κάμηλον διὰ τρυπήματος ῥαφίδος εἰσελθεῖν ἢ πλούσιον εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: palin de legō hymin, eukopōteron estin kamēlon dia trypēmatos rhaphidos eiselthein ē plousion eis tēn basileian tou theou.

i18n.en: And again I say to you, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God."

notes.official: 'the kingdom of God': one of only four places where Matthew does not write 'the kingdom of the heavens' (12:28; 19:24; 21:31, 43). A few late witnesses read *kamilon* 'rope' for *kamēlon* 'camel'; the critical text has 'camel', and the hyperbole is intended.

paragraphs.text: ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἐξεπλήσσοντο σφόδρα λέγοντες· Τίς ἄρα δύναται σωθῆναι;
paragraphs.translit: akousantes de hoi mathētai exeplēssonto sphodra legontes· tis ara dynatai sōthēnai;

i18n.en: And when the disciples heard it, they were exceedingly astonished, saying: "Who then can be saved?"

paragraphs.text: ἐμβλέψας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Παρὰ ἀνθρώποις τοῦτο ἀδύνατόν ἐστιν, παρὰ δὲ θεῷ πάντα δυνατά.
paragraphs.translit: emblepsas de ho iēsous eipen autois· para anthrōpois touto adynaton estin, para de theō panta dynata.

i18n.en: And Jesus looked at them and said to them: "With people this is impossible, but with God all things are possible."

paragraphs.text: Τότε ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν πάντα καὶ ἠκολουθήσαμέν σοι· τί ἄρα ἔσται ἡμῖν;
paragraphs.translit: tote apokritheis ho petros eipen autō· idou hēmeis aphēkamen panta kai ēkolouthēsamen soi· ti ara estai hēmin;

i18n.en: Then Peter answered and said to him: "Behold, we have left everything and followed you; what then will there be for us?"

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ὑμεῖς οἱ ἀκολουθήσαντές μοι ἐν τῇ παλιγγενεσίᾳ, ὅταν καθίσῃ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ θρόνου δόξης αὐτοῦ, καθήσεσθε καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐπὶ δώδεκα θρόνους κρίνοντες τὰς δώδεκα φυλὰς τοῦ Ἰσραήλ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de iēsous eipen autois· amēn legō hymin hoti hymeis hoi akolouthēsantes moi en tē palingenesia, hotan kathisē ho huios tou anthrōpou epi thronou doxēs autou, kathēsesthe kai hymeis epi dōdeka thronous krinontes tas dōdeka phylas tou israēl.

i18n.en: And Jesus said to them: "Amen I say to you that you who have followed me, in the regeneration, when the Son of Man sits on the throne of his glory, you also will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

notes.official: *en tē palingenesia* 'in the regeneration': *palingenesia* ('again-genesis') is used by the Stoics for the periodic renewal of the cosmos (Marcus Aurelius 11.1), by Philo for the world after the Flood, with Noah's family as 'leaders of the regeneration' (Mos. 2.65), and by Josephus for the restoration of the nation after the exile (Ant. 11.66); its only other NT use is the believer's rebirth (Titus 3:5). Here, with the Son of Man enthroned (cf. 25:31) and the twelve judging the tribes, it is the eschatological renewal of the world. The RSV ('the new world') and NRSV ('the renewal of all things') paraphrase; the line keeps the formal equivalent of the ASV and KJV, which leaves the term's range open (`palingenesia-the-regeneration-mt-19-28`; `son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: καὶ πᾶς ὅστις ἀφῆκεν οἰκίας ἢ ἀδελφοὺς ἢ ἀδελφὰς ἢ πατέρα ἢ μητέρα ἢ γυναῖκα ἢ τέκνα ἢ ἀγροὺς ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματός μου, ἑκατονταπλασίονα λήμψεται καὶ ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσει.
paragraphs.translit: kai pas hostis aphēken oikias ē adelphous ē adelphas ē patera ē mētera ē gynaika ē tekna ē agrous heneken tou onomatos mou, hekatontaplasiona lēmpsetai kai zōēn aiōnion klēronomēsei.

i18n.en: And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for my name's sake will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life.

notes.official: SBLGNT includes *ē gynaika* 'or wife', which Vaticanus, Bezae and NA28 omit and the Byzantine text includes. SBLGNT reads *hekatontaplasiona* 'a hundredfold'; Vaticanus and L read *pollaplasiona* 'many times as much', as in Luke 18:30 (`critical-text-baseline-and-byzantine-variant-recording-matthew`). 'eternal life' (`aiōnios-mt-25-41-46-eternal-vs-age-pertaining-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: πολλοὶ δὲ ἔσονται πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι καὶ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι.
paragraphs.translit: polloi de esontai prōtoi eschatoi kai eschatoi prōtoi.

i18n.en: But many who are first will be last, and the last first."

notes.official:
*Polloi de esontai prōtoi eschatoi kai eschatoi prōtoi* 'But many who are first will be last, and the last first'. The reverse form without 'many' closes the following parable at 20:16.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 4) cites the saying 'after Matthew 19:30' in the proverbial form « Les premiers seront les derniers et les derniers seront les premiers » (closer to 20:16) and reads it as meaning that 'the created will be creators as the creators were created'. The line follows the Greek of 19:30, including 'many'.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Textual variant: the critical text reads ὁ κτίσας ('he who created'); the Byzantine/TR text (KJV 'he which made them') reads ὁ ποιήσας.

Textual variant: SBLGNT reads μὴ ἐπὶ πορνείᾳ ('except for unchastity') and includes the final clause καὶ ὁ ἀπολελυμένην γαμήσας μοιχᾶται; Vaticanus and others read παρεκτὸς λόγου πορνείας ποιεῖ αὐτὴν μοιχευθῆναι ('except on the ground of unchastity, makes her commit adultery', assimilating to 5:32), and Sinaiticus, D and others omit the final clause. Also unglossed: πορνεία 'unchastity' vs. 'fornication' (KJV) vs. 'sexual immorality'.
editorial_questions_resolved.default_taken: except for unchastity … and he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery (SBLGNT)
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: SBLGNT followed; 'unchastity' consistent with published 5:32; B and א D readings recorded.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Textual variant (major): the critical text reads Τί με ἐρωτᾷς περὶ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ; εἷς ἐστιν ὁ ἀγαθός ('Why do you ask me about what is good? One there is who is good'); the Byzantine/TR text (KJV) reads Τί με λέγεις ἀγαθόν; οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ θεός ('Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God'), harmonizing with Mk 10:18 / Lk 18:19. Linked variant at 19:16: the Byzantine text reads Διδάσκαλε ἀγαθέ ('Good Master'), the critical text Διδάσκαλε ('Teacher').
editorial_questions_resolved.default_taken: Why do you ask me about what is good? One there is who is good (critical text)
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: Critical text followed at 19:16-17; Byzantine 'Good Master' / 'Why callest thou me good?' recorded.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: παλιγγενεσία (palingenesia): 'the regeneration' (ASV/KJV) vs. 'the renewal of all things' / 'the new world' (RSV) / 'the rebirth'. Unglossed; a cosmological term (Stoic and Philonic usage) on which interpretive readings diverge.
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: 'the regeneration' kept (formal equivalent); Stoic, Philonic, Josephan and Titus 3:5 senses in commentary.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Textual variants: (a) SBLGNT includes ἢ γυναῖκα ('or wife'), which Vaticanus, D and NA28 omit, and the Byzantine text includes; (b) SBLGNT reads ἑκατονταπλασίονα ('a hundredfold'), Vaticanus and L read πολλαπλασίονα ('many times as much', as in Lk 18:30).
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: SBLGNT 'or wife ... a hundredfold' followed; B D / B L readings recorded.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Canon-wording difference: πολλοὶ δὲ ἔσονται πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι καὶ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι ('many who are first will be last') is cited in TBWTT ch. 4 (« d'après Matthieu, XIX-30 ») in the proverbial form « Les premiers seront les derniers et les derniers seront les premiers », without 'many' (closer to 20:16). Draft follows the Greek.
editorial_questions_resolved.default_taken: But many who are first will be last, and the last first
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: Greek followed ('many who are first'); canon's proverbial form recorded in reception note.
